name: task-completion non-fragile anchor set
what_this_is: Twelve (critic model, task, repeat, answer bytes) cells whose 12-point perturbation family under `assets/rubrics/task-completion.yaml` is NON-FRAGILE — pass rate exactly 12/12 or 0/12, never straddling threshold 7. Eight are robust accepts of a correct answer; four are robust rejects of a wrong one. A rubric or critic-prompt edit that moves any of these twelve has broken something that was stable.

amended.why_this_file_rather_than_a_superseding_: The standing invariant is: do not retro-edit committed evidence. It holds here — every measurement in this file is untouched. What it protects is measurements from being refitted to conclusions. It does not protect a prose annotation that has become a live misdirection in the file operators actually open: this file is the one a future author reads before crediting a rubric edit, and it was telling them one reading of an ambiguous rule was the corrected one. The withdrawal is also carried in docs/eval.md's RB-P19 entry and in docs/eval-data/2026-08-12-rbp19b-guard2-both-readings-22-prompts.json, and nothing in git history is rewritten — the pre-amendment bytes are `b439053`'s.

caveats.text: `shop-compare` r2's `answer_correct: false` comes from `tool_trace`, not from the answer text the critic reads. Its ground truth is a property of the trace; the critic never sees the trace. The cell is a valid robust reject of a malformed answer, but it is NOT evidence that the critic judged correctness, and it is the weakest of the twelve. Do not offer it as a bar.

The 12 cells reduce to 9 DISTINCT ANSWER TEXTS. The accept side is 8 cells / 5 distinct texts / 3 tasks / ONE family: `structured-extraction` (three 14b `extract-contact` cells share byte-identical output). The reject side is 4 cells of empty or malformed garbage. NOTHING on the accept side exercises `file-nav` or `memory-recall` — i.e. this set has near-zero coverage of the format-deduction failure mode it was screened alongside (RB-P20). An edit that fixes that failure mode can pass all twelve of these and still be unmeasured.

Passing all 12 is NECESSARY and nowhere near SUFFICIENT. This set proves an edit did not break twelve stable cells. It proves nothing about whether the edit moved the cell it was written for — that still requires the perturbation bar on THAT cell reporting its family non-fragile (docs/eval.md, 'Crediting a rubric edit'). Green here is a floor, not a credit.

how_to_use.rule: AMENDED 2026-08-12, TWICE (procedure only, per RB-P24's second half and then per RB-P24 (1); no measured field changed either time). Before crediting any edit to `assets/rubrics/task-completion.yaml` or to a critic-facing contract string: (1) run `guard_first_pass` below and read what it refuses on; (2) re-run the perturbation family over these 12 cells (`command`, with the `--task` flags in `cell_selection`), READ ITS EXIT STATUS AGAINST `command_exit_status` — 3 is expected here since RB-P24 (1), and a 0 is itself a signal — and check every `expect_pass_rate` still holds; (3) diff the `guard_dropped` block of every violating cell against the one committed here, cell by cell, and check `guard_readings` still names the same points under the same readings. Any change in (2) OR (3) is a regression until explained. STEP 3 IS NOT OPTIONAL: `pass_rate` is deliberately the FULL family, so a guard-clean family can change shape underneath an unchanged `expect_pass_rate` and step 2 alone will pass it. The floor being green is not the same as the reason the floor is trustworthy being intact.
how_to_use.rule_as_committed: Before crediting any edit to `assets/rubrics/task-completion.yaml` or to a critic-facing contract string, re-run the perturbation family over these 12 cells and check every `expect_pass_rate` still holds. Any change is a regression until explained.

guard_first_pass.why: AMENDED 2026-08-12 (second amendment; procedure prose only, no measured field moved). AS COMMITTED THIS SAID: “`criticreplay` exits 0 in the default `warn` mode whether or not guard 2 fired — the only signals are a GUARD section on stdout and fields in the artifacts — so a CI job that reads the exit code cannot see a violation. That half of RB-P24 is OPEN and is a CLI-contract change, not a docs one.” THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE: RB-P24 (1) is implemented and closed (2026-08-12, branch `feat/rbp24-exit-code`). A `warn`-mode run that fired guard 2 on a (point, cell) it actually replayed now exits **3**, with every artifact still written. So the exit code carries the verdict and this first pass is no longer the only machine-readable signal. IT IS STILL PART OF THE PROCEDURE, for a reason that does not depend on the status: `--guard error` refuses BEFORE any request and exits 1, so it tells you the refusal LIST — which (point, cell) pairs are tainted — at zero spend, before you decide whether to spend 208 requests. A `3` from the second pass says the guard fired; this pass says on what, for free. Full contract, including what a `1` does and does not promise: docs/eval.md, RB-P24.
guard_first_pass.expected: IT IS EXPECTED TO REFUSE, and refusing is not this floor failing. Measured 2026-08-12 on this branch, it exits 1 before the first request and names, on 4b: `nav-prod-port` r0 — `P3-right-correct` shares ['right'] (whole-text ['right'], substitution-pair ['right']); `nav-release-bundle` r0 — `P2-asks-requests` shares ['for'] (whole-text [], substitution-pair ['for']); plus `nav-prod-port` r1, the non-anchor cell of `cell_selection`. On 14b: `recall-oncall-rotation` r1 — `P1-reviewer-relative` ['who'] and `P2-asks-requests` ['for']. Those are exactly the three violating anchors below and no others. A DIFFERENT refusal list means the manifest or a frozen task prompt moved and this file's guard data is stale: stop and re-derive it before crediting anything.

cell_selection.cost_correction: `cost` below is the committed 12-cell estimate and is left as committed. The actual runs are 8 cells x 16 = 128 requests on 14b and 5 x 16 = 80 on 4b, i.e. 208 requests for the pair against the 192 estimated, because of the extra 4b cell. Measured totals for the 2026-08-12 `rbp19b` pair: 128 + 64 requests and 22,973 tokens on the 4b arm (which ran the 4 anchors only).

how_to_use.cost: 12 cells x 16 requests = 192 requests; ~74k tokens at the measured 384 tokens/request for `A-asfiled`. No answerer, no tools, no suite run.
how_to_use.command_exit_status: ADDED 2026-08-12 (second amendment). **This second pass now EXITS 3, not 0, and 3 is the expected status here — it is not this floor failing.** The cells it runs over include the three violating anchors named in `guard_first_pass.expected`, which is deliberate: `warn` mode measures them and records the violation on every row, in the summary's guard block and in the printed GUARD section. Measured on both models' committed stage-2 transcripts with the `cell_selection` task flags (offline, scripted critic, real CLI, status read from a shell's `$?`): 4b -> 3, 14b -> 3. Before RB-P24 (1) both exited 0. WHAT TO DO WITH IT: treat 3 as “proceed to step 3” — diff the `guard_dropped` blocks cell by cell as the rule already requires. A **0** here means the guard fired on NOTHING, which over these cells means the manifest or a frozen prompt moved: stop, exactly as a different refusal list in the first pass means stop. A **1** means the run did not complete a measurement (its artifacts, if any, are partial); a **2** is a usage error; a **4** means it measured but could not write the summary file. `--violations-exit-zero` exists for a procedure like this one and would make the second pass exit 0 again — DO NOT pass it here: it would throw away the signal this step now has, and the expected-3 rule above is what replaces it.

measured_under.guard_note: AMENDED 2026-08-12 — prose only, see `amended`; no number below moved. Every cell's `guard_violations` was recomputed offline against all 22 frozen task prompts, NOT copied from the screen's §6 table. **The values recorded here are the SUBSTITUTION-PAIR reading** of spec §3.3 step 3, guard 2 — the symmetric difference of a point's own `from`/`to` word sets. That is one of TWO defensible readings and the spec supports each in a different sentence; the screen's §6 table is the other (WHOLE-TEXT: the symmetric difference of the base and perturbed TEMPLATE word sets, §3.3's operative Test sentence). The user's ruling of 2026-08-12 is that both are computed, both are reported, and NEITHER is wrong — the earlier text here, which called this set “the CORRECTED” one and said the screen “under-reported `P2-asks-requests`”, is WITHDRAWN. On these twelve cells the two readings differ on exactly one (point, cell) pair — `P2-asks-requests` on 4b `nav-release-bundle` r0, flagged by substitution-pair and not by whole-text — and the shipped decision rule is their UNION, which on these twelve equals the substitution-pair table exactly. So every value below is what the union gives too, and nothing here moves under either reading. Both readings are reproduced mechanically, per (point, cell), in docs/eval-data/2026-08-12-rbp19b-anchors-{14b,4b}-summary.json, whose `expect_pass_rate`, `measured_min`, `measured_max`, `fragile` and all three `guard_dropped` blocks match this file cell for cell. Where a cell violates, `guard_dropped` gives the family recomputed with the violating points removed; the verdict is unchanged on every one of the twelve. This file remains the floor; the live per-(point, cell) guard record is the `rbp19b` artifacts, which carry both readings as machine-readable fields. See docs/eval.md RB-P19.
